title: Protocol to study presynaptic protein synthesis in ex vivo mouse hippocampal slices using HaloTag technology
protocol: Prepare Hamilton syringe.
Disinfect Hamilton syringe with 70% ethanol.
Rinse Hamilton syringe multiple times with Milli-Q water.
Disinfect stereotaxic surgical setup and tools with 70% ethanol.
Wipe stereotaxic surgical setup and all tools with Kimwipe.
Pickup animals from the animal facility.
Prepare dental drill and surgical supplies in the surgical area.
Obtain betadine, premixed 0.9% saline solution, and 70% ethanol in 50 mL falcon tubes.
Prepare a small container with 10% bleach.
Fill the vaporizer with isoflurane.
Ensure oxygen is connected well and the general anesthesia setup is functional.
Place all sterilized tools on a sterile pad.
Gather ophthalmic ointment.
Prepare microinjector pump control.
Thaw −80°C Halo-actin reporter viral aliquots by placing them on wet ice.
Attach Hamilton syringe to stereotaxic setup according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Slowly load virus into the syringe, ensuring enough for all mice plus 20% extra.
Gently place a clean cage with top on a heating pad without bedding.
Anesthetize and mount mouse on stereotaxic apparatus.
Turn on oxygen flow to the isoflurane induction chamber.
Place the mouse in the induction chamber.
Turn on flow of isoflurane to 5%.
Wait for the mouse to become sedated.
Adjust flow from induction chamber and decrease from 5% to 3% isoflurane.
Gently remove mouse from chamber and mount onto the stereotaxic frame using bite bar.
Slide nose cone over mouse’s nose, then decrease the flow of isoflurane to 2%.
Pinch the hind paw to ensure proper sedation has been achieved before securing animal in the stereotaxic frame.
Gently adjust the mouse so that mouse head looks straight and level.
Gently progress the ear bars into the ear canal.
Press gently on top of head to make sure mouse does not move in response.
Place ophthalmic ointment on mouse eyes using sterile swab.
Expose the skull.
Gently shave the fur from the mouse head.
Sterilize the scalp by applying betadine on a cotton swab in circular motion.
Make a vertical incision with surgical scissors from the posterior to the eyes.
Splay each layer of tissue open for visibility.
Gently wipe the exposed skull with a sterile swab dipped in 70% EtOH.
Clean off any remaining muscle and tissue.
Drill a single bore hole through the skull at the determined injection site.
Inject lentivirus into the region of interest using dissection scope or magnification glasses.
Find bregma as a reference point for coordinates.
Determine x- and y-coordinates based on established parameters.
Lower the tip of the syringe to the skull surface at bregma.
Zero the microinjector pump control at bregma.
Measure z-coordinate by moving to lambda, 0.05 units higher than bregma.
Adjust nose cone height to achieve an angle of 0.05.
Pause drilling if slight bleeding occurs until it stops.
Raise syringe after recording the z-coordinate to avoid hitting the drill tip with the syringe.
Press button on microinjector and apply pressure until liquid bead exits Hamilton syringe.
Wipe away liquid bead with paper tissue and discharge into 10% bleach.
Gently advance needle to 2.0 ventral from dura after reaching brain’s surface.
Inject viral solution at a flow rate of 0.2 mL/min for a total volume of 1.5 mL/hemisphere.
Wait 7–8 minutes before withdrawing the needle over 1–2 minutes.
Suture two halves of the scalp using nylon suture (NFS-2).
Deliver 1 mL of normal saline for post-surgical fluid resuscitation.
Place mouse in recovery cage with heated pad underneath.
Clean up surgical area, disinfect and dispose of all material appropriately.
Gather tools and solutions for hippocampal dissection and slicing.
Prepare ice bucket.
Prepare NMDG solution.
Prepare ACSF.
Bubble NMDG and ACSF with carbogen (5% carbon dioxide, 95% oxygen) for at least 10 min on ice before starting.
Remove agar from fridge and cut block with blade.
Cut perpendicular to create a block.
Cut across to create a well.
Thinly slice bottom to create a lid.
Calibrate vibratome blade and set proper settings.
Expose the experimental animal to isoflurane until nociceptive reflexes expire.
Decapitate the animal in under 30 s.
Remove brain and put into ice cold NMDG cutting solution.
Isolate hippocampi.
Adjust isolated hippocampi on block.
Cut hippocampi using VT1200s vibratome at a thickness of 300 μm.
Fill the slicing chamber with ice-cold NMDG and fill the outer chamber of the vibratome with ice.
Transfer slices into ACSF-filled slice holding chamber containing plastic mesh fixed onto a ring.
Let the slices recover for at least 30 min in the slice holding chamber at room temperature before starting HaloTag labeling protocol.
Remove dye-conjugated HTL from the −20°C freezer.
Prepare a desired dilution of HTL in ACSF from stock solution in a 20 mL Pyrex beaker.
Add RT ACSF and start bubbling with carbogen in a 20 mL Pyrex beaker.
Add JF549-HTL to a final concentration of 100 nM.
Bubble for 10 min, then gently collect slices with a transfer pipette and place in the beaker containing dye cocktail.
Label slices for 1 h.
Gently remove slices from the dye cocktail after labeling and transfer to bubbling ACSF without picking up much solution.
Wash slices in ACSF for 30 min.
Add JF646-HTL (200 nM) to the bubbling ACSF beaker for labeling newly synthesized Halo-actin.
Label slices in the JF646-HTL containing ACSF for 1 hour.
Transfer labeled slices to a fresh ACSF beaker and wash out for 30 minutes.
Fix slices with 4% PFA in a 24-well plate overnight at 4°C.
Replace PFA with 1× PBS the next day.
Mount sections onto slides using ProLong™ Diamond Antifade Mountant with DAPI, taking care to avoid damage or folds.
Leave the slides in the dark at room temperature and let them cure overnight (10–12 hours).
Seal the slides with nail polish the following day, let dry.
Store sealed slides at 4°C.
Turn on the microscope and necessary lasers (561 nm and 647 nm laser lines) on the day of imaging.
Clean the 63× objective.
Set the microscope to Plan-Apochromat 63×/1.4 Oil DIC M27 with 1.8× zoom settings for imaging.
Keep threshold, laser power, and gain constant for each experimental group imaged.
Set pixel width and height to 0.049 μm.
Set voxel depth to 0.187 μm.
Locate the stratum lucidum.
Take z-stacks throughout axon bundle at similar depths.
Ensure boutons are captured in their entirety.
Set step size to optimal.
Take three z-stacks through the entire z-plane of the tissue where boutons are visible (one in CA3a, one in CA3b, and one in CA3c).
Image a depth of about 10 μm with a z-stack consisting of about 50 frames.
Process images using Airyscan.
Ensure acquisition settings remain identical between treatment groups and imaging days.
